title: Insights and the atlas
summary: A grounded machine report, a weekly report across your repositories, and an offline atlas of their state.
why: A report built from commands run today cannot re-pitch work that already shipped; one built from memory or old transcripts can.

items.title: /machine-insights
items.does: Installs a command for a grounded machine report: git across every repository, Temp and boot, scheduled tasks, disk and the Claude footprint, from commands run now.
items.why: Ground truth measured in the report itself cannot recommend work that is already done.

items.title: Machine report host file
items.does: Creates an example host file listing your repository roots, report folder and backup alias, to be copied and filled in locally.
items.why: The report needs your machine's layout, and that layout must never land in a public repository; an example file ships, the real one stays local.

items.title: /fleet-insights weekly report
items.does: Installs a weekly review command: a dive per repository, a cross-repository dive, an adversary per finding and a diff against last week.
items.why: A weekly look across all repositories finds what no single session can see.

items.title: Weekly report task
items.does: Installs weekly_report.py and a Friday 17:00 task that runs /fleet-insights once in the background, skips weeks that already have a report and fails a run that leaves no page.
items.why: The report has to appear without anyone remembering to start it.

items.title: Offline atlas
items.does: Installs atlas.py, which reads every repository in the roster read-only and writes one self-contained HTML page with branch, last commit, dirty count and next action.
items.why: One glance at every repository answers where things stand without opening each one.

items.title: Atlas refresh when idle
items.does: Registers a task that refreshes the atlas after about 10 minutes of idle and stops when you come back; it skips when nothing changed.
items.why: The map stays current without costing anything while you work.

items.title: Public-repository census
items.does: Installs pubrepo_census.py, a read-only scan of tracked files, commit subjects and tags for home paths, email addresses and token shapes.
items.why: What an outsider sees first is the history; a census before publishing finds what a code review misses.

items.title: Log of acts waiting on you
items.does: Adds the /done step that appends one line per item still waiting on you, so the weekly report can list them.
items.why: Acts only you can do (a login, a cable, a password) were forgotten once they scrolled out of the hand-off.
